name: India
note: Central Acts only. Succession in India is religion-dependent: the Indian Succession Act’s probate requirement does not apply to wills made by Muslims or Indian Christians, and property passing by survivorship does not vest in an executor, so intestate heirship (Hindu Succession Act 1956 and uncodified Muslim personal law) is not modelled here. The Guardians and Wards Act 1890 is omitted as it concerns minors. No digital-assets fiduciary statute was found in the Acts retrieved.

roles.name: Attorney under a power of attorney
roles.summary: An ordinary power. India has no durable financial power by default: the agency is terminated by either the principal or the agent dying or becoming of unsound mind.

assigned.event: Principal executes an instrument empowering a person to act in their name

ends.event: Principal revokes, agent renounces, or the business of the agency is completed
Either the principal or the agent dies or becomes of unsound mind, or the principal is adjudicated insolvent

transitions.event: Principal executes the power of attorney (Powers-of Attorney Act s 2)
Revocation by the principal, renunciation by the agent, or completion of the business (Contract Act s 201)
Either party dies or becomes of unsound mind, or the principal is adjudicated insolvent (Contract Act s 201)

roles.name: Agency coupled with an interest
roles.summary: The only Indian agency that survives the principal’s incapacity or death — and it does so to protect the agent, not the principal. Where the agent has an interest in the property that is the subject-matter, the agency cannot be terminated to the prejudice of that interest, and the Act’s own illustration says it survives insanity and death.

assigned.event: Authority is given to an agent who has an interest in the property forming the subject-matter of the agency

ends.event: Express contract providing for termination, or the interest ceasing; it is not ended by the principal’s insanity or death

states.label: Agency in force, agent has an interest
Continues through the principal’s insanity or death

transitions.event: Authority granted where the agent has an interest in the subject-matter (Contract Act s 202)
Principal’s insanity or death, which does not terminate this agency (Contract Act s 202 illustration (a))
Express contract permitting termination, or the agent’s interest ceasing (Contract Act s 202)

roles.name: Nominated representative
roles.summary: Anyone not a minor may appoint a nominated representative in writing on plain paper, or name one in order of precedence in an advance directive that also says how they wish, or do not wish, to be treated for mental illness.

assigned.event: Person who is not a minor appoints a nominated representative in writing, or names individuals in order of precedence in an advance directive

starts.event: On appointment in writing, signed or thumb-marked, the appointee having accepted

states.label: Appointed in writing or named in an advance directive

transitions.event: Appointment in writing on plain paper, or naming in an advance directive (Mental Healthcare Act ss 5, 14)
The representative acts for the person in relation to mental healthcare and treatment (Mental Healthcare Act s 14)
Revocation of the appointment (Mental Healthcare Act s 14)

roles.name: Limited guardian
roles.summary: Support comes first. A district court or designated authority may add a limited guardian only where the person has already been given adequate and appropriate support and is still unable to take legally binding decisions — and that guardian decides in consultation with the person.

assigned.event: District court or designated authority finds that a person given adequate and appropriate support is still unable to take legally binding decisions

starts.event: Further support of a limited guardian is provided, to take legally binding decisions on the person’s behalf in consultation with them

transitions.event: Adequate and appropriate support provided under the Act (RPwD Act ss 13, 14)
Court or designated authority finds the person still unable to take legally binding decisions despite support (RPwD Act s 14)
Death of the person (Indian Succession Act s 211)

roles.name: Executor
roles.summary: Probate is granted only to an executor appointed by the will. The executor is the deceased’s legal representative for all purposes and the property vests in them — but neither that vesting nor the need for probate applies uniformly: property passing by survivorship is excluded, and s 213 does not apply to wills made by Muslims or Indian Christians.

assigned.event: Testator appoints an executor by the will, expressly or by necessary implication

starts.event: On grant of probate; no right as executor can be established in court without it, subject to the exemptions in s 213(2)

transitions.event: Testator appoints an executor by will (Indian Succession Act s 222)
Probate granted; the executor is legal representative and the property vests in them (ss 211, 213)
Administration of the estate completed (s 211)

roles.name: Administrator
roles.summary: Where there is no executor, administration may be granted to any person who would be entitled to the whole or part of the estate. Like the executor, the administrator is the legal representative and the property vests in them.

assigned.event: Court grants administration to a person entitled to the whole or any part of the deceased’s estate

starts.event: On the grant of letters of administration; the administrator is legal representative for all purposes

transitions.event: Administration granted to a person entitled to the estate (Indian Succession Act s 218)
Administration completed; property having vested in the administrator as legal representative (s 211)

roles.name: Person authorising removal of organs
localNames: person lawfully in possession of the dead body
roles.summary: A donor may authorise removal in writing before two or more witnesses, at least one a near relative. Failing that, if the person expressed no objection in life, the person lawfully in possession of the body may authorise removal unless a near relative objects.

assigned.event: Donor unequivocally authorises removal in writing before two or more witnesses, at least one of whom is a near relative

starts.event: After death, the person lawfully in possession of the body must give reasonable facilities for removal, unless they believe the authority was revoked

ends.event: Removal carried out, or a near relative objects where the deceased left no authority

states.label: No authority; person lawfully in possession may authorise

transitions.event: Donor authorises removal in writing before two or more witnesses (THOTA s 3(2))
No authority given, and no objection expressed by the person in life (THOTA s 3(3))
Death; person lawfully in possession grants facilities for removal (THOTA s 3(2))
Person lawfully in possession authorises removal, no near relative objecting (THOTA s 3(3))
A near relative is believed to object (THOTA s 3(3))

poaDurableByDefault.note: An agency is terminated by either the principal or the agent dying or becoming of unsound mind. The only exception is an agency coupled with an interest, which protects the agent rather than the principal.

supportedDecisionMakingStatute.name: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, ss 13-14 — support first, limited guardianship only where support has not sufficed

probateGrantName.note: Probate is granted only to an executor appointed by the will; otherwise letters of administration. Section 213 does not apply to wills made by Muslims or Indian Christians.

organDonationModel.note: Removal needs the donor’s unequivocal written authorisation before two witnesses; failing that, the person lawfully in possession of the body may authorise where the deceased expressed no objection and no near relative objects.
